tur48-0: Is your child saying their heel hurts after running and jumping, are they limping or walking on tiptoe? Irritation of the growth area of the heel bone during the growth years is called Sever’s disease (medical name: calcaneal apophysitis). Although the name sounds alarming, it is a common, temporary condition related to growth; the heel pain goes away once growth is complete.

tur48-4: The tight Achilles tendon repeatedly pulls on the growth area of the heel bone and irritates it.

tur48-13: The collagen in the ligaments that support the joints is thought to be different, which makes the ligaments looser and more flexible; in most people the exact cause is not known.
tur48-14: Keeping a healthy weight, supportive shoes and, if needed, custom insoles reduce the load on the joints. In many countries insoles are provided by foot health specialists (podiatrists); this profession is not widespread in Türkiye. If you need insoles, you can choose, on your doctor’s or physiotherapist’s advice, a reliable provider that makes them individually after assessing your walking and foot posture, has good references and carries out regular follow-up checks. A warm bath or hot water bottle can ease stiffness.
tur48-15: Stand upright in front of a counter, holding on lightly with one hand if needed. Lift one foot; keep the knee of the standing leg slightly bent rather than locked back. As it gets easier, try without holding on or with your eyes closed; when you do, stay next to the counter, ready to hold on if needed. It improves joint position sense and balance.
tur48-16: If your joints already move too far, stretches that push them to the end of their range are generally not recommended. The aim is not to increase flexibility but to strengthen and protect the joints with the surrounding muscles. Children are also advised not to bend their joints excessively as a show or “party trick”. It is also advisable to avoid repeating the same movement for long periods.
